Task: unify entire-brain memory sync on the per-fact wire (COR-2233 + subs COR-2234, COR-2235, COR-2236).
This work gates the stable CLI release. The tickets are the spec; read all four first:
https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2233

Decision already made (do not relitigate): the per-fact upsert/delta-feed wire
(factsync/perfact.go, shipped in COR-2126) is the only long-term hosted sync path.
This reverses COR-2211's "keep local-gitmeta default" outcome. Consent story:
connecting a repo is the consent moment, so a hosted default on connected repos
does not violate ADR-P1-A no-implicit-egress. A durable brain memory records this
(recall "per-fact wire memory sync decision" on branch stable-release-readiness-plan).

Current state to change:
- `entire brain memories sync` on a connected repo defaults to local-gitmeta;
  hosted sync requires --memories-backend=http.
- Manual http sync drives the branch-head CAS wire (factsync.HTTPServer,
  /brain/facts + /brain/facts/advance, proposals queue). Connected background
  sync (hostedFactsSyncAndPull: daemon tick, session-end hook, connect) drives
  the per-fact wire. Two hosted wires.

Work, in order:
1. COR-2234 — connected repos: plain `memories sync` syncs over the per-fact
   wire by default. Honest exit code/output on failure (COR-2202 precedent).
2. COR-2235 — retire the CAS client path; manual hosted sync goes through the
   per-fact wire. Check docs/proposal-queue-repair.md and server consumers
   before deleting proposals-queue code; decide a deprecation window for the
   server endpoints.
3. COR-2236 — remove gitmeta as a default anywhere, sweep flags/help/status/
   docs/MCP descriptions. BLOCKED ON A DECISION FROM EVIS first: keep gitmeta
   as explicit opt-in for unconnected repos, or remove it entirely. Ask before
   implementing this one.

Hard constraints:
- ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS / LOCAL_ONLY suppress all hosted sync regardless of defaults.
- Existing --memories-backend values must not silently change meaning: removed
  values fail with a clear message or map with a one-time deprecation warning
  (precedent: ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_HOSTED, PR #390).
- Already-synced gitmeta refs must stay readable; define migration/read-only story.
- Help text must state the default backend and what connectedness changes.

Verify before finishing: focused Go tests for the sync paths, plus a manual run
of `memories sync` on a connected and an unconnected repo showing the new
defaults and honest failure output. Update the Linear tickets as you land each piece.

156	//	/api/v1/repos/../brain/facts
157	//
158	// collapses at any normalizing hop to /api/v1/brain/facts, a route the caller never
159	// asked for. repoid.Validate states the rule instead; because it also requires the id
160	// to equal its own escaped form, the id is concatenated raw here — PathEscape would
161	// be a no-op and hiding the check behind it is what made this look safe before.
162	//
163	// Returning an error (rather than a string) is deliberate: it forces every call site
164	// to refuse BEFORE http.NewRequest exists, so a rejected id costs zero egress.
165	func repoBasePath(repoID string) (string, error) {
166		if err := repoid.Validate(repoID); err != nil {
167			return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: %w", err)
168		}
169		return "/api/v1/repos/" + repoID, nil
170	}
171	
172	// ErrBranchTooLong is returned when the caller's branch name exceeds the hosted
173	// fact-set API's cap. It is a distinct sentinel so a caller can tell a client-side
174	// refusal (nothing was sent; fix the branch) from a server rejection.
175	var ErrBranchTooLong = errors.New("factsync: branch name is too long for the hosted fact-set API")
176	
177	// maxBranchBytes is the hosted fact-set API's cap on a branch name, in BYTES as the
178	// server counts them (not runes — a multi-byte name is longer on the wire than it
179	// looks on screen).
180	//
181	// This is the ONE server cap this client mirrors, and it is worth saying why, because
182	// mirroring a server-owned number is normally a bug waiting to happen: if the hosted
183	// cap is raised, a client that hardcoded the old one refuses branches the server would
184	// now accept, and no amount of error-body surfacing helps because the request is never
185	// made. Two things make this cap the exception:
186	//
187	//   - The round trip it saves is expensive and pointless. The branch is known before
188	//     a socket is opened, and the request that would learn the limit carries the
189	//     member's bearer token and, on Advance/Resolve, the member's whole fact set — a
190	//     multi-megabyte upload posted only to be told the branch name was too long.
191	//   - The number is not close to anything real. Git states no length limit of its own
192	//     on a ref name — the effective one is the filesystem's — and a branch anywhere
193	//     near 512 bytes is pathological rather than merely long, so nothing a member
194	//     would plausibly name a branch sits near this value.
195	//
196	// The residual risk is stated rather than hidden: if the hosted cap is RAISED, this
197	// client refuses a branch the server would now accept, and it cannot detect that on
198	// its own, because the request it would have learned from is the one it declined to
199	// make. Raising this constant is then the fix, and it is one line. That risk is
200	// accepted only because the value is far outside the range of real branch names; it is
201	// why no other server-owned cap is mirrored here.
202	//
203	// The other caps the hosted API grew at the same time are deliberately NOT mirrored:
204	// the artifact count and the manifest reference count on the publish path, and
205	// whatever the hosted MCP query surface applies to its own branch argument. The client
206	// has no independent basis for those numbers (unlike the publish body-size ceiling,
207	// which it must project anyway to avoid building a multi-GB buffer), and the hosted
208	// MCP branch is server-defaulted, so a guessed constant there would refuse requests
209	// the server accepts. Those are surfaced from the server's own error body instead —
210	// see internal/cli/publish.go and internal/hostedbrain/client.go.
211	const maxBranchBytes = 512
212	
213	// validateBranch refuses a branch the hosted API is known to reject, before the
214	// request exists.
215	func validateBranch(branch string) error {
216		if len(branch) > maxBranchBytes {
217			return fmt.Errorf("%w: branch is %d bytes, limit is %d", ErrBranchTooLong, len(branch), maxBranchBytes)
218		}
219		return nil
220	}
221	
222	// detail renders the server's objection with this client's own bearer token removed.
223	// Every non-2xx render on the fact-set and proposal surfaces goes through here, so
224	// the redaction is applied once rather than at each of the ten call sites. See
225	// httpx.Redact for why an echoed token has to be stripped even though the peer that
226	// echoed it already had it.
227	func (h *HTTPServer) detail(resp *http.Response) string {
228		return httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorSuffix(resp), h.Token)
229	}
230	
231	// conflict renders a 412/409 as ErrConflict, carrying whatever the server said about
232	// the head that moved.
233	//
234	// The SENTINEL is the contract: Sync and the proposal loops re-read and re-merge on
235	// errors.Is(err, ErrConflict), so a CAS loss must keep matching it no matter how the
236	// message grows. fmt.Errorf with %w preserves that; a plain formatted error would
237	// silently turn a converging retry into a failed sync. When the server said nothing
238	// the bare sentinel is returned unchanged, so a quiet 412 reads exactly as it did
239	// before this file learned to read bodies.
240	func (h *HTTPServer) conflict(resp *http.Response) error {
241		if detail := httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorDetail(resp), h.Token); detail != "" {
242			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrConflict, detail)
243		}
244		return ErrConflict
245	}
246	
247	// requestTarget is the single chokepoint for the two caller-supplied values that
248	// decide whether a fact-set request can possibly succeed: the repo id, which must be
249	// exactly one safe path segment (repoBasePath), and the branch, which must be within
250	// the hosted cap. Both are checked before http.NewRequest exists, so a request that
251	// cannot succeed costs zero egress.
252	func requestTarget(repoID, branch string) (string, error) {
253		// Repo id first: it is the check that keeps the request on the route the caller
254		// asked for, so when both values are bad that is the one worth reporting.
255		base, err := repoBasePath(repoID)
256		if err != nil {
257			return "", err
258		}
259		if err := validateBranch(branch); err != nil {
260			return "", err
261		}
262		return base, nil
263	}
264	
265	func (h *HTTPServer) newRequest(ctx context.Context, method, path string, body io.Reader) (*http.Request, error) {
266		// Scheme floor (apiurl.Validate) at the single request chokepoint of both the
267		// fact-set and the proposal-queue surfaces: the bearer token below and the
268		// fact-set blob above it must never be built into a plaintext request to a
269		// non-loopback host. Every construction path lands here, so a caller that
270		// bypassed the CLI's own check is still covered.
271		base, err := apiurl.Validate(h.BaseURL)
272		if err != nil {
273			return nil, fmt.Errorf("factsync: %w", err)
274		}
275		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, base+path, body)
276		if err != nil {
277			return nil, err
278		}
279		if h.Token != "" {
280			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+h.Token)
281		}
282		if body != nil {
283			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
284		}
285		return req, nil
286	}
287	
288	// Current reads the branch's fact-set head. A 200 with found=false (no head yet) returns
289	// found=false and nil plaintext; the data field is base64-decoded by encoding/json into
290	// the []byte. Any non-200 is an error (the runner cannot merge against an unknown state).
291	func (h *HTTPServer) Current(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch string) (string, []byte, bool, error) {
292		ref, plaintext, _, found, err := h.CurrentWithAuthors(ctx, repoID, branch)
293		return ref, plaintext, found, err
294	}
295	
296	// CurrentWithAuthors is Current plus the additive per-fact attribution map the
297	// hosted server stamps on the GET response (fact id → display handle). A server
298	// without the field yields a nil map — the sync contract is unchanged.
299	func (h *HTTPServer) CurrentWithAuthors(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch string) (string, []byte, map[string]string, bool, error) {
300		base, err := requestTarget(repoID, branch)
301		if err != nil {
302			return "", nil, nil, false, err
303		}
304		path := base + "/brain/facts?branch=" + url.QueryEscape(branch)
305		req, err := h.newRequest(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil)
306		if err != nil {
307			return "", nil, nil, false, err
308		}
309		resp, err := h.do(req)
310		if err != nil {
311			return "", nil, nil, false, fmt.Errorf("factsync: GET fact-set head %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
312		}
313		defer resp.Body.Close()
314		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
315			return "", nil, nil, false, fmt.Errorf("factsync: GET fact-set head %s/%s: unexpected status %s%s", repoID, branch, resp.Status, h.detail(resp))
316		}
317		var out struct {
318			Found   bool              `json:"found"`
319			Ref     string            `json:"ref"`
320			Version int64             `json:"version"`
321			Data    []byte            `json:"data"`
322			Authors map[string]string `json:"authors"`
323		}
324		if err := httpx.DecodeJSONBody(resp, &out); err != nil {
325			return "", nil, nil, false, fmt.Errorf("factsync: decode fact-set head %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
326		}
327		if !out.Found {
328			return "", nil, nil, false, nil
329		}
330		return out.Ref, out.Data, out.Authors, true, nil
331	}
332	
333	// Advance compare-and-swaps the head onto plaintext, mapping the endpoint's outcomes to
334	// the Server contract: 200 with changed → the new ref; 200 with changed=false
335	// or unchanged:true → ErrNoChange; 412/409 → ErrConflict. Any other status is
336	// an error (a 400 empty-data, 404 unknown repo, 503 unconfigured, or 5xx —
337	// none of which the runner should paper over). The duplicated ref spellings
338	// keep mixed-version entire-api / entire-brain rollouts compatible.
339	func (h *HTTPServer) Advance(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch, oldRef string, plaintext []byte) (string, error) {
340		base, err := requestTarget(repoID, branch)
341		if err != nil {
342			return "", err
343		}
344		reqBody := struct {
345			Branch       string `json:"branch"`
346			OldRef       string `json:"oldRef"`
347			OldRefLegacy string `json:"old_ref"`
348			Data         []byte `json:"data"`
349		}{Branch: branch, OldRef: oldRef, OldRefLegacy: oldRef, Data: plaintext}
350		buf, err := json.Marshal(reqBody)
351		if err != nil {
352			return "", err
353		}
354	
355		path := base + "/brain/facts/advance"
356		req, err := h.newRequest(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, bytes.NewReader(buf))
357		if err != nil {
358			return "", err
359		}
360		resp, err := h.do(req)
361		if err != nil {
362			return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: POST advance %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
363		}
364		defer resp.Body.Close()
365	
366		switch resp.StatusCode {
367		case http.StatusOK:
368			var out struct {
369				NewRef          string `json:"newRef"`
370				NewRefLegacy    string `json:"new_ref"`
371				Version         int64  `json:"version"`
372				Changed         *bool  `json:"changed"`
373				UnchangedLegacy *bool  `json:"unchanged"`
374			}
375			if err := httpx.DecodeJSONBody(resp, &out); err != nil {
376				return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: decode advance %s/%s: %w", repoID, branch, err)
377			}
378			if out.Changed != nil && !*out.Changed {
379				return "", ErrNoChange
380			}
381			if out.UnchangedLegacy != nil && *out.UnchangedLegacy {
382				return "", ErrNoChange
383			}
384			newRef := out.NewRef
385			if newRef == "" {
386				newRef = out.NewRefLegacy
387			}
388			if out.Changed == nil && out.UnchangedLegacy == nil && oldRef != "" && newRef == oldRef {
389				return "", ErrNoChange
390			}
391			if newRef == "" {
392				return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: decode advance %s/%s: missing new ref", repoID, branch)
393			}
394			return newRef, nil
395		case http.StatusPreconditionFailed, http.StatusConflict:
396			// The sentinel is the contract (sync.go re-reads and re-merges on
397			// errors.Is(err, ErrConflict)); the server's account of WHICH head moved is
398			// additive, and only when it said something.
399			return "", h.conflict(resp)
400		default:
401			return "", fmt.Errorf("factsync: POST advance %s/%s: unexpected status %s%s", repoID, branch, resp.Status, h.detail(resp))
402		}
403	}

1	// Package factsync is the runner-side read-merge-CAS loop that syncs a member's
2	// durable facts into the hosted, shared fact-set head. It is where the two P1.M2
3	// halves meet: the deterministic merge engine (factmerge) and the hosted
4	// atomic head (entire-api's FactSetStore, reached here through the Server seam).
5	//
6	// Per ADR-P1-E the MERGE runs on the runner (this package), not in the API server:
7	// the server only stores encrypted blobs and compare-and-swaps the branch head, so
8	// it never needs the cgo/SQLite-heavy brain merge core. Sync pulls the current head
9	// in plaintext, keep-both promotes the member's local facts into it via factmerge,
10	// and pushes the result back under CAS — retrying on a losing swap.
11	package factsync
12	
13	import (
14		"bytes"
15		"context"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"time"
19	
20		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge"
21	)
22	
23	// ErrConflict is what a Server.Advance returns when the head moved under it (a
24	// concurrent member advanced first) — the signal for Sync to re-read and re-merge.
25	var ErrConflict = errors.New("factsync: fact-set head changed (CAS conflict)")
26	
27	// ErrNoChange is what a Server.Advance returns when the merged blob is byte-identical
28	// to the current head — the member's facts were all already present. Sync treats it as
29	// "converged, nothing to publish", not an error.
30	var ErrNoChange = errors.New("factsync: fact-set unchanged by merge")
31	
32	// ErrExhausted is returned when Sync cannot land its merge within maxAttempts CAS
33	// tries — sustained contention the caller should retry later or escalate.
34	var ErrExhausted = errors.New("factsync: exceeded CAS retries")
35	
36	// maxAttempts bounds the read-merge-CAS loop so pathological contention fails loudly
37	// instead of spinning forever.
38	const maxAttempts = 32
39	
40	// Server is the runner's view of the hosted fact-set head (entire-api's FactSetStore
41	// over HTTP). Current returns the branch head's content ref and the DECRYPTED facts
42	// blob (found=false, nil blob when the branch has no head yet — merge into empty).
43	// Advance seals+stores the merged plaintext and compare-and-swaps the head from oldRef
44	// onto its content ref, returning ErrConflict on a losing swap and ErrNoChange when the
45	// merge produced exactly the current content.
46	type Server interface {
47		Current(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch string) (ref string, plaintext []byte, found bool, err error)
48		Advance(ctx context.Context, repoID, branch, oldRef string, plaintext []byte) (newRef string, err error)
49	}
50	
51	// Result reports the outcome of a Sync: whether the head advanced (Published), the new
52	// content ref, how many CAS attempts it took, and any review Proposals the keep-both
53	// merge queued (cross-member conflicts a human must resolve — the M2.4 surface).
54	type Result struct {
55		Published bool
56		NewRef    string
57		Attempts  int
58		Proposals []factmerge.Proposal
59	
60		// Facts is the fact set this sync settled on: the merged content when the CAS
61		// won, or the head as read when it converged with no change. The runner already
62		// computed it, so a caller needing the post-sync head (to check which proposals
63		// are still live, or to mirror settlements into local facts) can use this
64		// instead of issuing another Current — one fewer network round-trip per sync.
65		Facts []factmerge.Record
66	}
67	
68	// Sync runs the read-merge-CAS loop: pull the head, keep-both promote local into it via
69	// factmerge, push under CAS, retry on ErrConflict. `now` is injected for determinism.
70	// memberID identifies the syncing member; it is stamped onto every review Proposal the
71	// merge raises (ProposedBy) so a cross-member conflict is attributable and routable.
72	// A keep-both merge NEVER silently drops a member's fact (ADR-P1-G): identical facts
73	// (same content id) union their provenance; genuine conflicts are kept and queued as
74	// routed Proposals in the Result (resolve them with Resolve).
75	func Sync(ctx context.Context, srv Server, repoID, branch, memberID string, local []factmerge.Record, now time.Time) (Result, error) {
76		if memberID == "" {
77			// A blank memberID would stamp ProposedBy="" (dropped by omitempty), making a
78			// cross-member proposal indistinguishable from a local one — routing lost. Reject.
79			return Result{}, errors.New("factsync: memberID is required (proposal routing)")
80		}
81		// Redact local-only provenance coordinates before these facts leave for the shared
82		// head — no member's local filesystem path leaks cross-member (opaque ids are kept,
83		// so provenance still unions). Copies; the caller's local facts are not mutated.
84		local = SanitizeForEgress(local)
85		// Verify this member's own facts BEFORE publishing them. The head check below
86		// fails closed, so one malformed record reaching the shared head would break
87		// every other member's sync — a failure the member that produced it should
88		// take, and take here, rather than exporting it.
89		if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentities(local); err != nil {
90			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("factsync: local fact set for %s/%s is not publishable: %w", repoID, branch, err)
91		}
92		for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ {
93			ref, plaintext, found, err := srv.Current(ctx, repoID, branch)
94			if err != nil {
95				return Result{}, err
96			}
97			var head []factmerge.Record
98			if found && len(plaintext) > 0 {
99				head, err = factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(plaintext))
100				if err != nil {
101					return Result{}, err
102				}
103				// The head is written by every member with push access, so nothing about
104				// it is authenticated by having arrived over the transport. Re-derive each
105				// record's content id before merging: without this, a record carrying
106				// ANOTHER member's id with attacker-chosen text makes Promote's id match
107				// read as "already present, union the provenance", silently discarding the
108				// victim's real statement and keeping the forgery — with the victim's own
109				// anchors attached to it. Fail closed rather than merge a head one record
110				// of which is provably not what it claims to be.
111				if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentities(head); err != nil {
112					return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("factsync: shared fact-set head for %s/%s is not trustworthy: %w", repoID, branch, err)
113				}
114			}
115	
116			// Cross-member merge is structurally cross-branch promote: the member's local
117			// facts are the "source" promoted (keep-both) into the current head "target".
118			merged, proposals, _ := factmerge.Promote(local, head, "keep-both", branch, now)
119			// Promote only carries ACTIVE source facts, so a member's RETIREMENTS
120			// (a `facts retract`, or a supersede they applied in review) never reach
121			// the head on their own: the head keeps listing the statement as active,
122			// Advance sees byte-identical content and reports "no change", and every
123			// other member goes on reading a statement its owner declared false.
124			// Carry them over explicitly. Nothing is deleted — the record and its
125			// provenance stay and only the status is retired — so the keep-both
126			// guarantee (ADR-P1-G) holds.
127			merged = applyLocalRetirements(local, merged, now)
128			// Stamp routing: every conflict this member's sync raised is attributed to it.
129			for i := range proposals {
130				proposals[i].ProposedBy = memberID
131			}
132	
133			var buf bytes.Buffer
134			if err := factmerge.WriteNDJSON(&buf, merged); err != nil {
135				return Result{}, err
136			}
137			if buf.Len() == 0 {
138				// The merge produced an EMPTY fact-set (an empty head and no active local
139				// facts to promote). There is nothing to publish — a head always points at
140				// content, and Advance rejects empty plaintext — so report converged rather
141				// than push an empty blob. (A non-empty head can never merge to empty: promote
142				// only grows the target.)
143				return Result{Published: false, NewRef: ref, Attempts: attempt, Proposals: proposals, Facts: merged}, nil
144			}
145	
146			newRef, err := srv.Advance(ctx, repoID, branch, ref, buf.Bytes())
147			switch {
148			case err == nil:
149				return Result{Published: true, NewRef: newRef, Attempts: attempt, Proposals: proposals, Facts: merged}, nil
150			case errors.Is(err, ErrNoChange):
151				return Result{Published: false, NewRef: ref, Attempts: attempt, Proposals: proposals, Facts: merged}, nil
152			case errors.Is(err, ErrConflict):
153				continue // a concurrent member advanced first — re-read the newer head and re-merge
154			default:
155				return Result{}, err
156			}
157		}
158		return Result{}, ErrExhausted
159	}
160	
161	// applyLocalRetirements folds a member's non-active local facts onto the merged
162	// set: a record the shared head still lists as active is retired to the status
163	// its owner gave it, carrying the SupersededBy pointer. It only ever moves a
164	// fact from active to retracted/superseded — it never revives one and never
165	// removes one — so the merge stays monotone and a second sync of the same local
166	// state is a no-op.
167	func applyLocalRetirements(local, merged []factmerge.Record, now time.Time) []factmerge.Record {
168		for _, l := range local {
169			if l.Status != factmerge.StatusRetracted && l.Status != factmerge.StatusSuperseded {
170				continue
171			}
172			i := factmerge.IndexOf(merged, l.ID)
173			if i < 0 || merged[i].Status != factmerge.StatusActive {
174				continue
175			}
176			merged[i].Status = l.Status
177			merged[i].SupersededBy = l.SupersededBy
178			merged[i].UpdatedAt = now
179		}
180		return merged
181	}

COR-2234 and COR-2235 are done and in review; COR-2236 is blocked on your decision, laid out at the bottom.

## What landed — PR [#452](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/452)

- **COR-2234**: plain `memories sync` on a connected repo now syncs over the hosted per-fact wire by default. The transport-security tests (body limits, token redaction, https floor, repo-id segment rule, retries, fuzz) were retargeted to the per-fact methods, not dropped. `local-gitmeta` and the CAS `Server` seam stay for unconnected repos pending COR-2236.
- **Server-side check**: in the entire monorepo (@90dfe547f), the gateway routes only `/brain/facts` (upsert + feed) to brainstore — the `advance`/`proposals` endpoints no longer exist server-side. This client was their last consumer, so there is no deprecation window to decide.
- Both Linear tickets are In Review with detailed comments; COR-2233 is In Progress. Decisions recorded as brain memories.

## Two things you should know

1. **Design change found during manual verification.** With `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` set, a connected repo's plain sync now **skips loudly** instead of falling back to local-gitmeta. When I tried the fallback on this repo, the keep-both merge against the stale gitmeta head re-raised **1365 spurious conflict proposals** into your local review queue. The kill switch suppresses sync; it shouldn't redirect it. I removed that queue file afterward — it contained only the 1365 entries from my run, so your local brain is back to its pre-run state.
2. **Breaking surface** (pre-stable, noted in the PR): `memories sync --json` for hosted runs now reports upsert counts/feed totals instead of CAS head/proposal fields, and `memories proposals` is gone.

## Verification

Full `go test ./...` green, gofmt/vet clean (no oxfmt config exists in this repo — CI uses gofmt). Manual runs with the dev binary: connected repo → `synced … via hosted (https://aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io): …; feed facts=2276 kept=1546`, exit 0; unconnected temp repo → `via local-gitmeta (…)`, exit 0, zero egress; unreachable hosted target → named pull failure, exit 1; connected + NO_EGRESS → skip message, zero egress.

## COR-2236 — your call before I implement

Gitmeta is the only no-egress memory-sharing path for repos not connected to brainstore. Options:

1. **Remove gitmeta entirely** — unconnected repos get local-only memories; sharing requires connecting. Smallest stable-release compat surface, but needs a story for already-synced gitmeta stores, and `--memories-backend=local-gitmeta` must fail with a clear message.
2. **Keep gitmeta as explicit opt-in** (`--memories-backend=local-gitmeta`), no default anywhere — an unconnected plain sync would then refuse with "connect or pass a backend" instead of silently syncing locally.

My recommendation is **option 2**: it keeps existing gitmeta stores readable and writable with zero migration work, and today's stale-head incident argues against gitmeta *defaults*, not against its explicit use on never-connected repos. Which way do you want it?
